methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $8.6B.

private.name: Archer Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $3.33B

data.narrative:
Joby Aviation, a publicly traded autonomous aircraft manufacturer in the Drones & Autonomous sector, carries a current valuation of $6.86B following capital raises exceeding $2B. The peer universe comprises eight private companies, including Series D through Series H stage firms such as Wayve ($8.6B), Zipline ($7.6B), Nuro ($6.0B), and fellow public-stage Archer Aviation ($3.3B).

Peer-median analysis across four same-sector comparables with similar valuation tier positioning yields a median implied valuation of $6.8B, with a stated range of $3.3B to $8.6B. This method anchors the primary triangulation input given limited publicly comparable data in the autonomous vehicle segment. The peer set reflects heterogeneous stages—Series D through public markets—which introduces variance but also captures the breadth of capital market valuations for this technology sector.

Triangulated analysis across available methodologies supports a valuation range of $5.8B to $7.8B, centered on $6.8B. The current market valuation of $6.86B aligns precisely with the peer median, indicating consistency with observable market pricing for functionally similar stage and sector positioning. Key uncertainties include the wide valuation dispersion across peers ($3.3B to $8.6B), reflecting differing technology maturity and commercialization timelines, and the limited depth of public comparables for direct reference.
